title: Go SDK: streaming cancellation windows and resumable-stream strategy
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Customers embedding long-running streaming responses (chat + tool-calls, long embeddings) are hitting opaque cancellations in the Go SDK. Two frequent user problems: (1) client routines cancel due to local deadlines (context.WithTimeout) while the backend still has usable progress, and (2) automatic retries restart the entire generation which causes duplicate side-effects and excessive cost.

Goal: Implement an ergonomic, correctness-first streaming cancellation model for the Go SDK that: (a) clearly distinguishes soft/interruptible deadlines from hard kill deadlines, (b) propagates cancel reason metadata to the server when possible, and (c) supports a resumable-stream token model so idempotent clients can continue progress after transient interrupts without re-running side-effectful actions.

Why different from prior tickets: Existing streaming work focused on deadline propagation and graceful shutdowns (cancel semantics), but we have not provided a first-class resumability token + cancellation-window model that composes with the SDK's retry and backoff layer. This ticket adds that surface, example usage patterns, and tests for back-compat and safety.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce 'CancellationWindow' API in Go SDK that lets callers declare a soft window (duration) and an absolute hard deadline; SDK converts soft window into a polite interrupt signal and hard deadline into a hard Cancel() propagated to transport.

When a soft interrupt occurs, the SDK attaches a 'X-Stream-Interrupt-Reason: soft_deadline' header and continues to accept (and buffer) a short grace period for server to flush partial segments; client receives a dedicated event (StreamEventInterrupted) that includes whether resume is supported.

Add resumability token flow: when server supports resumability, responses include 'resume_token' frames; SDK exposes Resume() which resumes from token and coordinates with retry/backoff to avoid double-execution of side effects.
Retries that attempt resume must be idempotency-aware: non-idempotent routes must not auto-resume; SDK exposes boolean RouteSupportsResumability and honors it.

Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering: soft -> resume success, soft -> resume failure (fallback to restart), hard deadline preemption, interaction with client-side context cancellation, and concurrency stress tests for 1000 short streams.
Doc examples in repo: two runnable examples under examples/streams/resumable and examples/streams/interruptible_timeout demonstrating recommended patterns.
No API breaking changes for callers not opting into new APIs.
Benchmarks: median end-to-end additional latency for soft-window handling < 5ms at p50, added memory < 1MB per stream on average for buffered partial segments.
Design and security review notes added to PR and accepted (security_review_required: true).
technical_notes:
Design summary:
1) CancellationWindow model: caller supplies (softWindow time.Duration, hardDeadline time.Time). When softWindow elapses the SDK sends a polite interrupt control frame to server and emits StreamEventInterrupted to the caller. The stream remains open for a small grace window (default 150ms) to allow server to flush; after grace window elapses SDK issues transport-level Cancel/Close.
2) Resume token: server may send a base64 resume token frame; SDK persists it in memory and exposes Resume(token) which establishes a resume RPC that supplies the previous KV/cache hint. Resume establishes a transient idempotency lock with server; server returns resume success/failure.
3) Retry integration: existing retry middleware gets a new 'ResumeAttempt' branch. When network or soft interrupts happen and a resume token exists and route is marked resumable, the middleware will attempt a single resumable retry with exponential backoff starting at 50ms. Non-idempotent routes (e.g., 'tool-call') will be labeled in model route metadata and resume is disabled by default.
4) Context propagation: the SDK will still respect ctx cancellation; context cancellation is treated as a hard immediate deadline unless the caller opts into CancellationWindow and uses ctxWithWindow(ctx, soft, hard). This avoids surprising behavior where ctx timeout silently restarts generation.
5) Telemetry: new event types: stream.interrupt.soft, stream.interrupt.hard, stream.resume.attempt, stream.resume.success, stream.resume.failure. These are emitted to Console and included in per-request traces.

Server compatibility: protocol changes are additive (optional frames). We will gate resumability feature on server version >= 1.18 using capability handshake.
implementation_plan: Week 1: API design and RFC (small design doc + examples) + security checklist
Week 2: Implement CancellationWindow primitives, grace-window handling, and transport header changes
Week 3: Implement resume token parsing, Resume() API and basic middleware path
Week 4: Retry middleware integration, add idempotency flags and route metadata checks
Week 5: Tests: unit, integration with local server mock, perf benchmark, docs and examples
Week 6: PR review, address feedback, merge and cut go-sdk patch release
risks: Resumability semantics are subtle for side-effectful routes; risk of accidental double-execution if route metadata is incorrect.
Memory usage for buffering flushed partial segments could regress under high concurrency if not bounded; need strict caps and eviction policy.
Server must support protocol frames for full resume; otherwise resume attempts will fail and SDK must fall back cleanly.
Telemetry volume growth if we emit too-detailed interrupt/resume events per token; sampling strategy required.
test_plan: Unit tests for CancellationWindow behavior (soft -> event emitted, grace window respected, hard -> immediate cancel)
Integration with server mock that simulates resumable and non-resumable flows
E2E test: resume success path where server continues from token and returns remaining tokens; verify no duplicate side-effects recorded
Stress: 1000 concurrent short streams with soft windows to validate memory cap and latency numbers
Fuzz: random timeouts and partial network failures to ensure no resource leaks
Compatibility test: when server does not advertise resumability, SDK falls back with no changes to existing behavior
rollout_plan: Feature is opt-in behind Go SDK vX.Y flag 'EnableResumableStreams'. Initial rollout: enable for internal canary apps and 5 customer beta tenants. Monitor metric set: stream.resume.success_rate, stream.resume.latency, stream.interrupt.rate and memory_per_stream. If resumability success_rate < 90% or memory regression > 15% trigger rollback. After 2 weeks of stable metrics, flip default to on for all hosted API customers on non-tool-call routes.
dependencies: SEC-104 (security review for resumed state tokens and retention)
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Thompson: Initial write-up — created ticket and draft design. Marked as P1 because multiple enterprise customers reported cost spikes when streams restarted repeatedly.

2026-03-11 Ravi Patel: Left notes on API ergonomics during sync: prefer ctxWithWindow helper rather than changing base ctx cancellation semantics. Added a small example for caller pattern where they want a soft window but still allow ctx cancel to abort immediately.
2026-03-11 Priya Singh (Security): Reviewed possible attack surface for resume tokens — requested tokens be short-lived and scope-limited; added SEC-104 dependency.
2026-03-11 Anya Lopez (PM): Suggested labeling routes in the model catalog as 'resumable: true/false' to avoid accidental resume on tool-calls. Added PM-398 for docs and migration notes.

2026-03-12 Ravi Patel: Pushed initial prototype branch for CancellationWindow and grace buffering: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/812 — benchmarked locally, low overhead. Calling out two TODOs: implement token persistence for long-running clients; add sampling for telemetry.
2026-03-12 QA: Requested integration test that simulates server delay > grace window to ensure hard cancel path works correctly and resources are released.
